parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, same-sex conduct legal since 1990, and no documented traveler-facing universal exposure (no facility ban, no birth-sex custody rule, no border/marker-screening practice, no hotel-refusal pattern). Positives reaching visitors: 2016 health-ministry social-name resolution and 2022 mental-health non-discrimination law, which suggest emergency care is not birth-sex-gated. Against that: no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse, and reports describe frequent violence and discrimination against LGBT people that police often ignore — a documented impunity pattern, tier 3 on the ladder, not tier 1 or 2 state targeting. State-adjacent hostility (school discussion ban, book-burning rhetoric, capital council banning a trans memorial) and low public acceptance reinforce thin recourse. Resident-only gaps (no LGR, marriage, adoption) are discounted as climate. Lands at Elevated Risk, mid-band, well above universal-exclusion dossiers.
